sites.rationale: EP1 has no endogenous signal peptide; its N-terminus (residues 1–37) is extracellular and its C-terminus (355–402) is intracellular, making the N-terminus the sole extracellular terminus. The published construct places BRIL immediately before EP1 residue 1 (M), corresponding to insert_after_residue=0. The 37-residue extracellular N-terminal domain provides ample clearance from TM1 (which begins at residue 38). L2 corroborates the N-terminal placement explicitly. Since no specific residue number is named in either clip, position is topology-derived. Full-length human EP1 receptor (residues 1–394) engineered with an exogenous HA signal peptide followed by a BRIL (thermostabilized apocytochrome b562RIL) domain fusion at the N-terminus; construct expressed and used for cryo-EM structural characterization (PMC12107139). The HA signal peptide drives ER targeting and is cleaved, leaving BRIL at the extracellular N-terminus of the membrane-anchored receptor.

sources.claim: The human EP1 receptor (residues 1 to 394) was engineered with an N-terminal HA signal peptide and BRIL fusion for enhanced expression.

literature_notes: Only two ledger lines are available (L1, L2), both from the same paper (PMC12107139) and describing the same N-terminal BRIL fusion construct. No ledger evidence supports insertions in ECL1 (97–111), ECL2 (178–200), or ECL3 (320–332); those sites cannot be proposed. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are reported in the ledger. BRIL (~106 aa) is larger than the 13–23 aa ALFA-tag range specified, but the site itself is validated for domain-level insertion tolerance at the extracellular N-terminus.
